title: Baby Blues or Something More?
hook: Weepy and overwhelmed in the first days is common and usually passes within two weeks. When low mood lingers and disrupts daily life, it may be postpartum depression — common and treatable.
key_points: Baby blues — tearfulness, mood swings, anxiety — affect many new parents and tend to lift within about two weeks.
Postpartum depression or anxiety lasts longer and gets in the way of daily life and bonding with your baby.
It's common and not a personal failing — about 1 in 8 birthing parents report postpartum depression symptoms.
Partners can experience it too, and it's very treatable; screening and reaching out for help matter.
content_html: In the first days after birth, many new parents feel weepy, anxious, and on edge — the so-called baby blues. They're extremely common and usually lift on their own within about two weeks. When that low or anxious mood lingers, deepens, and starts getting in the way of daily life or bonding with your baby, it may be postpartum depression or anxiety.
extra_html: The CDC notes that postpartum depression is more intense and lasts longer than the baby blues, and that about 1 in 8 birthing parents report symptoms — so it is common, not a personal failing. It can look like crying more than usual, anger, or feeling distant from your baby. Importantly, partners and non-birthing parents can experience it too, and it is very treatable. Screening and speaking up help, so tell your provider how you're really doing. This is general guidance — reach out to your doctor or midwife; in the U.S. you can call or text the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline at 1-833-852-6262 (1-833-TLC-MAMA), and if you have thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, seek help immediately or call 988.

related.title: Healing After Birth Takes Weeks, Not Days
related.hook: Your body just did something huge, and recovery is a season, not a single appointment. Bleeding, cramps, healing, and mood shifts are all part of the fourth trimester.

related.title: You Can't Pour From an Empty Cup
related.hook: Looking after yourself isn't a luxury — it's part of caring for your baby. A rested, supported parent has more patience and presence to give.

flashcards.prompt: How do baby blues differ from postpartum depression?

choices.text: Baby blues usually lift within ~2 weeks; depression lasts longer and disrupts daily life
They're the same thing with different names
Baby blues last for months; depression clears up in a few days

flashcards.explanation_html: Baby blues are common and short-lived, easing within about two weeks. Postpartum depression is more intense, lasts longer, and interferes with everyday life.

flashcards.prompt: Is postpartum depression a sign of being a bad or weak parent?
flashcards.back_html: No. It's a common medical condition — about 1 in 8 birthing parents report symptoms — and it is not a personal failing. It is very treatable, and help works.

flashcards.prompt: Who can be affected by postpartum depression?

choices.text: Birthing parents and their partners alike
Only people with a prior mental health diagnosis

flashcards.explanation_html: Partners and non-birthing parents can experience postpartum depression too, so support and screening matter for the whole family.
